title: Indian Navy Repels Pirate Boarding of MV Golden Arsenal in Gulf of Aden
detail: The St. Vincent & Grenadines-flagged bulk carrier Golden Arsenal (21 crew including 1 Indian national), en route from Aden to Somalia roughly 300nm ENE of Djibouti in the Gulf of Aden, was boarded by four armed pirates carrying RPGs. The crew locked themselves in the ship's citadel; pirates damaged the bridge but could not breach it. INS Trikand and MARCOS commandos, backed by a P-8I patrol aircraft, responded, the pirates fled, and the vessel was secured and resumed its voyage with no injuries reported. It was the first attempted hijacking since MT Eureka's seizure in early May, with the three previously hijacked vessels (Honour 25, Sward, MT Eureka) still held.

media.caption: Maritime Executive (Jul 2026): Pirates board and damage vessel then pursue second ship in Gulf of Aden

title: US Tells AU It Will End Funding Support for AUSSOM's UNSOS Logistics Backbone After Dec 31, 2026
detail: In a July 1 letter to the African Union, the United States said it will not support the UN Support Office in Somalia (UNSOS) — the logistics backbone (fuel, medevac, food, engineering, contingent-owned-equipment reimbursement) for the roughly 12,000-troop AUSSOM mission — beyond AUSSOM's current mandate expiry on December 31, 2026, and will oppose any UN Security Council renewal that includes UNSOS support. Washington cited Somalia's failure to take ownership of its own security despite roughly $2 billion in UNSOS support plus $1.6 billion in bilateral aid over the past decade. The AU Commission convened an emergency meeting on AUSSOM's future in response; a senior African diplomat called the US decision 'irreversible' — a major threat to the security architecture propping up the federal government against Al-Shabaab, landing directly atop the ongoing constitutional crisis.

media.caption: ChimpReports (Jul 1, 2026): Crisis as US moves to end support for UN Somalia mission
